title: The Gamble
subtitle: The loser is left with nothing, the winner takes all.

trails.title: Religious Reform
trails.description: This book isn't a history text, but the change in writing style suggests that there was a change in authors.

items.text: The Gamble
Chapel of Our Lady of Sorrows
The master of the manor sighs.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: All this time waiting for Zeno. I really want nothing more than to clear up this little misunderstanding of ours.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: There's no benefit to me hurting you. I hope only to peacefully return you to your friends and, in return, receive mine.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: After all, this city and its false era will be washed away by the "Storm" before long.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: *sigh* Those poor unbelievers. We were all once like them, yet to realize that we are children bathed in the light of the divine.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: One day, they will turn from darkness to light, just like our Zeno friends did not long ago.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: The apostates, however, they who have abandoned our faith, they must die.
Heretics and oath breakers, the most detestable of all.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: I'm still curious, you know, about who attacked the manor.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: Who disturbed the meeting between the Apostles Brotherhood and the messenger of the great Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: Who came here?
He kicks a small stone at his feet.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: And took away my people?
The potion has locked the blind doctor's throat. She cannot speak.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: I wouldn't be surprised if Marcando's already messed things up in the favela, but ...
He turns his back to the doctor.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: As long as he continues to recruit young arcanists, it doesn't matter.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: People like him are useful.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: Tools to be used to our benefit until they're lost to the "Storm."

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: Isn't that also how Zeno uses their soldiers, Doctor? As currency to be spent and lost?
A chip may roll away from the gambling table, but it will only find itself at another.
All the world's a casino, and all the men and women merely chips. We have no choice but to take our place at the table.
He looks at the doctor.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: At least Manus Vindictae promises these soldiers a future, a future worth looking forward to.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: The Sufferer will be reborn.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: And the Apostles Brotherhood will sail south with me. We will become followers of the Sufferer, undertake THEIR trials, and THEIR grace will be bestowed upon us.
He leans close, whispering in her ear.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: And with THEIR blessing, no matter how many times the world is reversed, we will stand firm.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: For we will be immortal.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: Yesterday is within our reach, dear lady.
The Colonel's Manor
Lopera crouches in the bushes by the manor, observing the guards' movements. The place is surprisingly light on security.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Seven, maybe eight, guards? No way to get through. Damn!
Cautious footsteps approach from behind.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Who's there?!

items.speaker: Mr. Duncan
items.text: Oh, sweet Mary, I finally found you! Haha! I bet you didn't expect to see me here, did you?
An unexpected ally.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Duncan? How did you know I was here?!

items.speaker: Mr. Duncan
items.text: Shh, keep it down now. Our friends at the Veterans' Residence told me everything.

items.speaker: Mr. Duncan
items.text: The Timekeeper said you were going to the manor alone.

items.speaker: Mr. Duncan
items.text: My, would you look at the beautiful greenery. Are you heading to that chapel?
Amidst the distant greenery, just past the building before them, peeks the chapel's bell tower.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Yeah. If the doctor's in there, I have to find a way to break in.

items.speaker: Mr. Duncan
items.text: Do you have any plans? Reinforcements?

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Reinforcements? No time for that. Just watch. I can handle this myself.
The path to the chapel is well within the sights of the patrolling guards.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Unless you dare to join me, old-timer?
The old veteran answers with action.
He lowers his sunglasses and lifts his blowpipe.

items.speaker: Mr. Duncan
items.text: Give me a few darts.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Okay. Here's the plan: you lure the guards away, and I'll check inside the chapel.
She tilts her crucible and, in the flame of an arcane skill, produces a few poison darts. She hands them to the old man.

items.speaker: Mr. Duncan
items.text: Alright. When I take my shot, I'll head that way. You stay hidden in the woods and make your way to the other side.
He crouches, aiming at an unfortunate guard's neck.
*thwip*
The guard drops instantly.

items.speaker: Brotherhood Guard
items.text: Intruder! Over there!
Alarm sirens blare.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Lead them toward the river.
Duncan catches the smoke bomb tossed by Lopera.

items.speaker: Mr. Duncan
items.text: Let's make this a little more exciting, shall we, boys?
He lobs the bomb, aims his blowpipe, and pierces the bomb in midair.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Nice shot!
With the guards distracted, Lopera raises her guns and makes her way to the chapel.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: Ah. It appears someone has come to your rescue, dear lady.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: I'm not surprised.
Santos gazes at the doctor. He holds a small control button in his hand.
He has no qualms about reducing this place to a pile of rubble.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Doctor!
Her shout echoes through the halls of the chapel.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: Huh? It's you!
The little gambler from the ship.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: I should've put a bullet in your skull back on that ship.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: I'm afraid you're playing the wrong game now.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Oh, yeah? So what does the winner get this time? Dr. Dores?
She steps toward the enemy on the pulpit.
Santos spreads his arms.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: No, there are no prizes.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: You and I are nothing but specks of dust in the wind.
Guns emptied, Lopera drops her revolver and charges at her opponent with nothing but her fists.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Looks like I win again.
She kicks the weakened Santos to the ground, pinning him by the throat, her fist poised.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: Yes, yes, you won this round.
He lies among the rubble, blood trickling from his mouth, smiling as Lopera's fist hovers above him.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: But I'm afraid there won't be a table left to play the next.

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: So long, little gambler.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: What?!

items.speaker: Santos
items.text: Perhaps it's time you paid a little more attention to your friend.
He presses the button in his hand. After a loud bang, the chapel starts to crumble.
In Lopera's moment of distraction, Santos kicks her away.
He vanishes amid the chaos of the explosion.
Now there is no one but Lopera, the doctor, and a building that's about to crush them both.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: Crap!
She grits her teeth and runs to the pulpit, freeing the bound doctor.
She tries to speak, but the effects of the potion still hold her throat in a tight grip.

items.speaker: Lopera
items.text: We can talk after we get out of here.
She hoists the doctor onto her back and carries her through the falling debris.
TO BE CONTINUED…
